The Rally Brief · September 24, 2026

The morning picture

Two developments set the morning agenda. A federal judge has temporarily ordered the White House to restore access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico, moving a fast-developing press-access dispute into its next legal phase. President Donald Trump is also hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping today, with trade, artificial intelligence and the Iran war among the issues surrounding the summit.

Judge temporarily restores White House access

U.S. District Judge Tim Kelly ordered the administration early Thursday to restore White House access for journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico while their lawsuit proceeds. Reuters reports that Kelly said the ban was likely unconstitutional; the Associated Press describes the ruling as a temporary block on the administration's action.

The distinction matters: this is an interim court order, not a final resolution of the constitutional dispute. The three organizations sued after their journalists were denied access following President Trump's September 18 announcement.

Reuters: Court blocks the White House ban →

Trump and Xi meet at the White House

Trump welcomes Xi to the White House Thursday for a summit expected to focus on managing U.S.-China competition rather than producing a sweeping settlement. Reuters reports that the agenda includes trade and technology issues against a backdrop of tensions over Taiwan and Iran. The meeting follows an extension of the two countries' tariff truce.

Artificial intelligence is one concrete thread to watch. U.S. officials recently proposed a bilateral mechanism for notifying each other about significant AI incidents. A proposal is not an agreement, and any summit language will matter more than expectations going into the meeting.
